scope: Independent read-only static review of frozen rolling storage bounds/publication/seek accounting; no runtime, Apache equivalence, performance or production qualification

actor_source.claim: Actor/watch/admission/lifecycle source byte-identical to qualified07 baseline

checks.name: retained index and transient allocations
checks.finding: Limits checks ceil(entryCount/interval) sparse checkpoint capacities for every segment, descriptor/table capacities,128bytes per entry for active+replacement+Journal growth, four checkpoint bundle buffers, bounded cleanup names and fixed overhead. Journal reserve_index uses try_reserve_exact with capacity capped at max_index_entries; it does not permit unconstrained geometric capacities. Corrupt cache reads are capped by the DATA-derived expected bundle length.

checks.name: disk publication and replacement
checks.finding: Actual enumerated file lengths include old/new data, sidecars and temp manifests; disk reservation precedes mutations. Roll verifies old data and syncs new files before durable manifest selection, then admits new append. Replacement copies/validates exact old data and protects both generations through manifest rename+directory sync; cleanup follows. I/O publication failure poisons the selected owner.

checks.name: file descriptors and payload scratch
checks.finding: Store validates aggregate per-store index/disk ceilings and documents max_stores active files plus four transient actor files. Sealed reads use one transient CheckedCursor. Source/destination replacement handles drop before replacement validation/index/publication. At most one maximum-entry validation/scan payload is additional to normalized work and append copy; allocator/OS/caller outputs are separately disclosed.

checks.name: hidden seek work reaches wire request budget
checks.finding: CheckedCursor open reads protected24-byte header and file metadata, not a full journal recovery. It seeks a previously data-certified checkpoint. Every skipped/returned payload and entry is charged through segments::Work -> Partition.read_with_work -> Store.read_entry -> FetchBudget.read. A scan-only FetchBudgetExceeded becomes distinct ScanBudget and ScanLimit, preventing successful output truncation or a false miss after hidden budget exhaustion. Entry counts separately bound fixed entry/file headers.

checks.name: offset and timestamp seek semantics
checks.finding: Containing atomic inputs retain their complete bytes, and Fetch still filters older complete batches. Time checkpoint selection uses strict prefix_max<wanted, retaining equal and nonmonotonic timestamps before the desired record; per-segment maximum controls skipping. Returned cursor entries receive payload CRC and range/record validation.

checks.name: actor cancellation and mutation ordering
checks.finding: Metadata actor source is unchanged from07. Store.append marks change on confirmed append or new poison; Store reads mark new poison. The actor takes changes and publishes watch version before replying, including canceled/lost receipts. Delete/Produce identity ordering, capture-before-enqueue, retained admission through outside-actor wait, stop/drain/join behavior remain in the unchanged actor.

documentation_refinements_resolved: Seek byte budget now explicitly means payload bytes, with entry caps bounding fixed headers
Config now names the additional bounded maximum-entry validation/scan payload and distinguishes monolithic64-byte slots from rolling index envelopes
limitations: Static review does not execute the frozen candidate
Runtime fault histories, independent Apache observations and raw-WAL/index parsing must retain their own exact-source receipts
Legacy monolithic proof cannot qualify rolling layout
No retention, compaction, replication, power-loss or performance claim
